static_traits.name: Zhou Liya
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with colleagues affected, seen as not serious enough; has a roommate to talk with but has not yet communicated about this issue
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness, no past psychotherapy experience
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, capable of self-reflection, highly cooperative, positive attitude; speech rate not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: I constantly feel unable to take anything in life seriously, thus using humor as a defense mechanism.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize my inability to be serious, and that always using humor as a defense may hinder my goals; hence seeking counseling.
growth_experiences: Since adolescence, gradually forming a pattern of using humor to avoid serious engagement in serious or stressful situations; in recent months this pattern has clearly intensified, evolving into almost always joking and finding it hard to have serious conversations.

There is a gap between the long-term ideal and reality (hoping to 'change the world', while in reality engaging in factory work), together with work pressure, bringing frustrating and tense experiences, strengthening the habit of using humor to buffer pressure.

core_beliefs: I am a person unable to take things seriously
If I invest seriously, I will fail and disappoint others

special_situations.event: In the factory, the supervisor gives a serious talk about deadlines
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I respond seriously, others will see my nervousness and inadequacy, thinking me unreliable; using humor can defuse embarrassment and pressure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately telling jokes in serious situations, easing the atmosphere, displacing the topic
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: As long as I make them laugh, they will not see how nervous I am

special_situations.event: When facing challenges and responsibilities in work or life
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I take these challenges seriously, I might fail and disappoint people
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using humor to downplay the importance of events, avoiding in-depth discussion and direct coping
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am never able to take things seriously

special_situations.event: When planning to invest more seriously in goals and responsibilities
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Taking things seriously means greater risk: once I fail, I will disappoint others
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces investment and uses joking self-mockery to buffer possible failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I get serious, I will fail and disappoint others

special_situations.event: After being told by the supervisor 'you need to be more serious'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others' criticism shows that I am essentially not good enough and not reliable enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using humor and self-mockery to cover embarrassment and shame, avoiding further serious exchanges
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This shows I am simply someone not to be taken seriously

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be treated as a reliable and trustworthy person, to be taken seriously, and to realize self-worth through serious commitment
core_conflict.fear: Fearing that getting serious will lead to failure, being judged, disappointing others, thus exposing one's inadequacy
defense_goal: Maintaining distance and a sense of control through humor, buffering anxiety and shame, avoiding negative evaluation

object_relations.self_representation: A nervous person, worried about inadequacy being seen through, needing to cover it with humor
object_relations.object_representation: Serious and judgmental others (e.g. supervisors, colleagues) who may be disappointed and negate

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When an authority figure (such as a supervisor) has a serious talk or makes demands or gives feedback
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The other person is judging whether I am reliable; if I get serious, my inadequacy will be exposed and negated (transference: projecting the past fear of being judged onto the current relationship)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle and empathic tone, name the tension behind the humor and the fear of being judged, invite staying with the present feeling: for example, 'Just now you used a joke to ease the atmosphere, and I also felt you were a bit nervous; can we look together at what this nervousness is trying to protect you from?'

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When a more serious commitment and action regarding goals or responsibilities is needed
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Being serious equals greater failure risk and disappointing others
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: With a steady pace, concretizing questioning, guiding emotional connection: 'When you think about investing seriously, what feelings arise in your body? Let us not solve it yet; just notice that fear together.'

manifestations: The gap between the ideal of hoping to 'change the world' and the reality of factory work triggers frustration
Downplaying serious topics with humor, struggling to invest in meaningful conversation and action
outcomes: Hard to have meaningful communication and deal with important issues
Seen by others as not serious enough

manifestations: Avoiding serious investment with humor when facing responsibilities and choices
Worries that once I choose seriously I must bear responsibility for failure
outcomes: Declined self-evaluation with feelings of frustration and anxiety

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, the opposite of 'acceptance'.
manifestations: Displacing attention with jokes in serious or stressful topics and situations, avoiding direct contact with problems and emotions
Using humor to ease tension, bypassing the fear of being judged or failing

positive_force: Fairly good self-awareness; actively recognized and described the pattern of humor as defense
Has motivation to change, clearly hoping to be taken seriously and achieve goals
Humor helps buffer stress and build connections to some extent
Positive attitude; willing to do self-monitoring (such as keeping a diary)
negative_force: High worry about failure and disappointing others
Over-relying on humor to avoid in serious/stressful situations, forming a fixed response
Cognitive distortions such as overgeneralization, mind reading, personalization
Long-term frustration and work pressure from the gap between reality and the ideal (changing the world)

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding serious communication and investment by joking / using humor in serious or stressful situations
antecedent: Supervisor holds a serious talk or sets deadline demands
When facing challenges and responsibilities in work or life
Occasions requiring serious communication with colleagues or others
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying that serious investment will lead to failure and disappointing others, accompanied by marked nervousness and anxiety, thus buffering and covering with humor
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome emotions (nervousness, shame, being judged), and avoiding potential negative evaluation
target_behavior.consequence: Work performance affected; seen by colleagues and supervisors as not serious enough; struggling to have meaningful conversations and handle important issues
